name: Vibratory Urticaria

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Vibratory Urticaria

criteria.description: Development of localized wheals and erythema within minutes of vibratory stimulus
Positive response to standardized vibration provocation test reproducing symptoms
Exclusion of other physical urticarias and systemic causes
Demonstration of histamine release from mast cells upon vibratory stimulation (supportive laboratory finding)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of vibration-triggered wheals and positive vibration provocation test with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by provocation testing; histamine release assays may aid confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized pruritic wheals induced by vibration
Erythema at sites of vibratory stimulus
Transient burning sensation following vibration exposure

common.symptomName: Cutaneous angioedema localized to vibrated areas
Mild systemic flushing after intense vibration
Pruritus persisting for up to 1 hour post-stimulus
searchTerms: itch lasting up to an hour

common.symptomName: Mast cell mediator-related symptoms such as headache or lightheadedness
searchTerms: headache or dizziness from allergic mediators

occasional.symptomName: Urticarial lesions spreading beyond vibrated area
Mild respiratory discomfort following vibration exposure
Transient hypotension associated with severe episodes
searchTerms: temporary low blood pressure during episodes
fainting risk from low BP in episodes

rare.symptomName: Anaphylaxis triggered by intense vibratory stimuli
Syncope related to systemic mast cell activation
searchTerms: loss of consciousness during allergic episodes

laboratory: Elevated serum histamine levels following vibratory provocation
Increased plasma tryptase during acute episodes
other: Positive vibration provocation test reproducing wheals and erythema

distinguishingFeatures: Lesions induced by stroking or scratching rather than vibration
Wheals appear within minutes after mechanical pressure
Triggered by cold exposure rather than vibration
Triggered by heat, exercise, or emotional stress
Smaller punctate wheals with surrounding erythema

redFlags: Rapid onset of systemic symptoms including hypotension or syncope
Airway swelling or respiratory distress following vibration exposure
Signs of anaphylaxis requiring emergency intervention
references: Boyden SE et al. Vibratory urticaria is caused by mutations in ADGRE2. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2016.
Kaplan AP. Physical urticarias. Allergy Asthma Proc. 2012.
